# torchsim/torch-sim (commit 17c14a054c9857d326f6974abe804829aeb1e285)
# torchsim/torch-sim Overview
[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides an atomistic simulation engine for high-performance molecular dynamics, structural optimization, and static calculations. It leverages PyTorch for efficient computation, particularly for machine learning interatomic potentials.

The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) data structure serves as the engine's central container for atomistic system properties. It represents systems as PyTorch tensors, enabling batched operations and direct GPU computation. [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management) provides further details on [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121).

High-level runner functions orchestrate simulation execution. These functions include [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) for molecular dynamics, [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) for geometry relaxations, and [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844) for single-point calculations. These runners abstract away complexities and manage trajectory reporting. [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) discusses these functions further.

The engine includes a suite of PyTorch-accelerated molecular dynamics integrators. They support the time evolution of atomistic systems under NVE, NVT, and NPT ensembles for batched simulations with periodic boundary conditions. [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators) covers these implementations.

Geometry optimization algorithms relax atomic structures to minimize system energy. This includes Gradient Descent, FIRE, BFGS, and L-BFGS, supporting batched operations and cell optimization through a filter-based design. [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms) provides a detailed discussion of these optimizers.

An autobatching system dynamically manages GPU memory and optimizes batch processing for diverse simulation scenarios. It efficiently groups multiple atomistic systems and dynamically handles their convergence. [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms) offers more information.

Multiple neighbor list implementations efficiently identify interatomic interactions within a specified cutoff. An automatic fallback mechanism ensures optimal performance by prioritizing available hardware-accelerated solutions and providing pure PyTorch alternatives. [Neighbor List Algorithms](#neighbor-list-algorithms) provides further details.

The framework includes a variety of models for calculating interatomic energies, forces, and stresses. These range from classical potentials, such as Lennard-Jones, to wrappers for external machine learning potentials. All models adhere to a common interface for consistent integration. [Model Implementations and Integration](#model-implementations-and-integration) describes these models.

Tools for calculating correlation properties enable analysis of simulation dynamics and transport phenomena. This includes general time correlation functions, velocity autocorrelation, and heat flux autocorrelation, computed using FFT-based methods with PyTorch acceleration. [Advanced Physical Property Calculations](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-advanced-physical-property-calculations) and [Simulation Property Calculators](#simulation-property-calculators) cover these capabilities.

Auxiliary functionalities support the core engine, including applying constraints, converting to and from external atomistic file formats (e.g., ASE, Pymatgen), and providing specialized mathematical utilities. [Auxiliary Simulation Functionalities](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-auxiliary-simulation-functionalities) elaborates on these.

Reproducibility mechanisms ensure deterministic simulation trajectories. This involves explicit seeding of the [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40) within [`SimState.rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44) and consistent batch composition for stochastic integrators and batched simulations. [Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-ensuring-reproducibility-in-torchsim) provides detailed guidance.

The User Guide section [User Guide to Core Concepts](#user-guide-to-core-concepts) offers a high-level overview of these fundamental concepts for new users.

## Atomistic Simulation Engine Core
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) project provides an atomistic simulation engine that leverages PyTorch for high-performance molecular dynamics (MD), structural optimization, and static calculations, particularly for machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). The engine's core design allows for GPU acceleration and automatic batching of simulations.

Central to the engine's operation is the management of simulation states. The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass serves as the fundamental container for atomistic system properties such as atomic positions, masses, and cell parameters. This design enables efficient batched operations, including cloning, splitting, and slicing of states. [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management) provides further details on [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121).

High-level runner functions orchestrate simulation execution, handling molecular dynamics simulations, geometry optimizations, and single-point energy calculations. These runners integrate with various models and manage trajectory reporting. More information on these functions can be found in [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners).

For MD simulations, the engine supports diverse integrators, including NVE (constant energy, volume), NVT (constant temperature, volume), and NPT (constant pressure, temperature) ensembles. These integrators are implemented to handle batched simulations and periodic boundary conditions, utilizing PyTorch for acceleration and managing unit conversions. [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators) covers these implementations in depth.

Geometry optimization tasks are handled by a suite of algorithms such as Gradient Descent, BFGS, L-BFGS, and FIRE (Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine). These optimizers are designed for batched atomic structure relaxations and incorporate a filter-based approach to manage cell optimization constraints and parameterizations. [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms) provides a detailed discussion of these optimizers.

To enhance performance, the engine incorporates autobatching mechanisms that manage GPU memory and optimize batch processing, especially for systems of varying sizes. These mechanisms dynamically handle the convergence of optimization tasks. Refer to [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms) for more information.

Beyond core simulation functionalities, the engine offers auxiliary capabilities, including the application of constraints (e.g., fixing atoms or the center of mass), conversion to and from external atomistic file formats like ASE and Pymatgen, and specialized mathematical utilities for tensor operations. These are detailed in [Auxiliary Simulation Functionalities](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-auxiliary-simulation-functionalities).

The engine also supports advanced physical property calculations, such as the computation of elastic tensors, Monte Carlo swap simulations, and correlation analyses like Velocity AutoCorrelation and Heat Flux AutoCorrelation functions. These capabilities are elaborated in [Advanced Physical Property Calculations](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-advanced-physical-property-calculations).

### Core Simulation State Management
The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass serves as the foundational data structure within TorchSim, encapsulating all essential properties of atomistic systems in a PyTorch-native format. This design allows for batched operations, where multiple distinct atomistic systems can be processed simultaneously on a GPU, significantly enhancing computational efficiency.

A [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object stores core attributes such as [`positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L177), [`masses`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L178), [`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179) (lattice vectors), [`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180) (periodic boundary conditions), [`atomic_numbers`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L181), and [`system_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L182). The [`system_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L182) is particularly important for managing batched simulations, as it identifies which atoms belong to which system within a single concatenated tensor. Additionally, [`_system_extras`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L184) and [`_atom_extras`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L185) provide flexible storage for arbitrary system-level and atom-level data, allowing for custom properties to be associated with the simulation state.

The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) provides a suite of methods designed for efficient manipulation of these batched systems. Operations like [`clone`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L591) create independent copies of the state, while [`to`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L730) facilitates moving the state to different PyTorch devices (e.g., CPU to GPU) or changing data types. For managing individual systems within a batch, [`split`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L690) divides a batched [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) into a list of single-system [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects, and [`pop`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L701) removes a specified system from the batch. The [`__getitem__`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L746) method enables slicing the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to extract subsets of systems or atoms. The [`concatenate_states`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1317) utility function also allows for combining multiple [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects into a single batched state.

The integration of [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) with molecular dynamics constraints is handled through [`Constraint`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L28) objects. These constraints, detailed further in [Auxiliary Simulation Functionalities](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-auxiliary-simulation-functionalities), modify the behavior of atoms or systems by adjusting positions, momenta, or forces. The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object can hold and apply these constraints, ensuring that simulated dynamics adhere to specified conditions, such as fixing atoms in place or maintaining the center of mass. The [`detach_state_graph`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1006) function is crucial for preventing memory leaks by detaching computational graphs when systems are removed or modified, particularly during dynamic batching operations.

To ensure broad compatibility, TorchSim provides utility functions in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py) for converting [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects to and from external atomistic simulation formats. This includes seamless conversion to ASE [`Atoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L26), Pymatgen [`Structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L10), and Phonopy [`PhonopyAtoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L5) objects, and vice versa. This interoperability allows users to leverage existing tools and data formats while benefiting from TorchSim's high-performance capabilities. The [`initialize_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1480) factory function simplifies the creation of a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) from these various external inputs, providing a unified entry point for setting up simulations.

### High-Level Simulation Runners
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) package provides high-level runner functions that abstract the complexities of orchestrating molecular dynamics simulations, geometry optimizations, and single-point calculations. These runners serve as primary entry points for executing atomistic simulations, managing state, and reporting results. They are designed to leverage automatic batching for performance and integrate trajectory reporting for data persistence. These functions are located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py) and exposed at the top level of the package via [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/__init__.py).

The three main runner functions are:

*   **[`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317)**: This function is responsible for performing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. It takes an initial simulation state, a chosen integrator (e.g., NVE, NVT, NPT), and a model (for energy/force calculations) as input. It then advances the simulation for a specified number of steps, applying the selected integrator's rules to evolve the system's positions and momenta. The [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) function uses a [`TrajectoryReporter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L68) to log simulation data at regular intervals, enabling post-simulation analysis. For efficiency, it employs a [`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475) to group systems into fixed batches, ensuring optimal utilization of GPU resources during the MD run. More details on the available integrators can be found in [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators).

*   **[`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638)**: This function orchestrates geometry optimizations, seeking to find stable atomic configurations by minimizing the system's energy. It requires an initial simulation state, an optimizer (such as Gradient Descent, BFGS, L-BFGS, or FIRE), and a model. The optimization process continues until a predefined convergence criterion is met, typically when forces or energy changes fall below a certain threshold. A key feature of [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) is its use of an [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768), which dynamically manages batches of systems. This allows the runner to efficiently process multiple optimization tasks simultaneously, removing systems from the batch as they converge and potentially adding new ones, thereby maximizing throughput. The module also provides utility functions, such as [`generate_energy_convergence_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L612) and [`generate_force_convergence_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L572), to help define these convergence criteria. For a deeper understanding of the optimizers, refer to [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms).

*   **[`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844)**: This function performs single-point calculations, which involve evaluating the energy, forces, and stress for a given atomic configuration without evolving its state over time. It takes a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) and a model as input and returns these computed properties. The [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844) function is often used as a preliminary step in more complex workflows or for analyzing specific snapshots from a simulation. It leverages the underlying model's capabilities to compute these properties efficiently, including support for batch processing.

All three runners are designed to interact with a [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) [Model Interface and Composition](#model-implementations-and-integration-model-interface-and-composition) for energy, force, and stress calculations, making them highly flexible with respect to the interatomic potential used. They manage [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management) that encapsulate atomistic system properties, handling transformations and updates across simulation steps. The autobatching mechanisms, specifically [`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475) and [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768) [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms), play a crucial role in optimizing performance by intelligently managing GPU memory and processing varying system sizes.

### Autobatching Mechanisms
Autobatching in TorchSim optimizes GPU memory usage and computational efficiency by dynamically managing batches of atomistic simulation states. This is particularly important because simulation states, characterized by properties like the number of atoms, can vary significantly in their memory footprint. The framework provides mechanisms to estimate memory requirements and adjust batch sizes accordingly, preventing out-of-memory errors and maximizing GPU utilization.

The core of TorchSim's autobatching capabilities is found in the [`autobatching`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L16) module ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py)). It includes functionalities for estimating the GPU memory consumed by a model's forward pass, which is then used to determine the maximum number of simulation states that can be processed concurrently. This estimation leverages memory scaling metrics such as the number of atoms ([`n_atoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L428)), the product of atom count and density ([`n_atoms_x_density`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L79)), or the actual number of neighbor list edges ([`n_edges`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L89)), offering flexibility based on the model's computational dependencies.

Two primary autobatching strategies are implemented to suit different simulation workflows:

*   **[`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475)**: This strategy pre-allocates simulation states into fixed batches. It is designed for scenarios where all input states need to undergo the same number of simulation steps, such as in molecular dynamics runs where the batch composition remains constant over time. The [`to_constant_volume_bins`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L46) function ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py)) groups states by their estimated memory usage into bins, optimizing packing efficiency similar to bin packing algorithms. Once batched, the [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) runner function leverages this for efficient, static batch processing. See [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) for more details.

*   **[`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768)**: This mechanism dynamically manages batches, particularly useful for iterative processes like geometry optimization where states converge at different rates. It can "hot-swap" converged states out of a batch and replace them with new, unconverged states. This dynamic approach ensures that GPU resources are continuously utilized by active simulations. The [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) runner function uses [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768) to efficiently manage systems during geometry optimizations, dynamically removing converged systems and adding new ones until all systems have reached their convergence criteria. This process also prevents memory leaks by detaching the computational graph of completed states. See [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) for more details.

Both batchers operate on [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects, which are designed to support efficient concatenation and splitting, enabling seamless manipulation of batched data. The [`determine_max_batch_size`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L195) function ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py)) is crucial for both strategies, finding the largest possible batch size that fits in GPU memory using an iterative search, while also implementing memory safety measures like releasing the CUDA caching allocator to avoid memory fragmentation. This adaptive approach ensures that TorchSim simulations are both memory-efficient and performant across a wide range of system sizes and computational models.

### Auxiliary Simulation Functionalities
This section covers the auxiliary functions that support the core atomistic simulation engine, providing capabilities for managing simulation constraints, facilitating data exchange with external atomistic simulation packages, and offering specialized mathematical operations for tensor manipulation.

The constraint system, defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py), allows for the application of various restrictions on atomic systems during simulations. This includes [`FixAtoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L444), which keeps specific atoms stationary, [`FixCom`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L522), which maintains the center of mass for a system, and [`FixSymmetry`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L777), which preserves the spacegroup symmetry of a crystal structure. These constraints influence how forces, momenta, and positions are adjusted during simulation steps, enabling the study of systems under specific physical conditions. For example, [`FixSymmetry`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L777) can be initialized from a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to refine its symmetry using external tools, then used to symmetrize forces, positions, and stress tensors during optimization or dynamics. The system handles constraints in a batched manner and includes utilities like [`merge_constraints`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L403) for combining constraints from multiple states and [`validate_constraints`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/constraints.py#L714) for ensuring their proper configuration.

For interoperability with other atomistic software, the I/O module ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py)) provides conversion functions between [`ts.SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L40) objects and representations from packages such as ASE ([`atoms_to_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L259), [`state_to_atoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L39)), Pymatgen ([`structures_to_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L363), [`state_to_structures`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L126)), and Phonopy ([`phonopy_to_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L449), [`state_to_phonopy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L202)). These functions facilitate the import and export of structural data, including atomic positions, cell parameters, and periodic boundary conditions, often handling additional system- or atom-specific metadata. This ensures that [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) can easily integrate into existing computational workflows that rely on these established libraries.

Advanced mathematical utilities, particularly for matrix operations, are crucial for many physics-based calculations within the engine. The [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py) module offers specialized functions like [`expm_frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L30) for computing the Fréchet derivative of the matrix exponential, which is essential in certain optimization and integration schemes. It also includes [`matrix_log_33`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L707) for calculating the matrix logarithm of 3x3 matrices, which is optimized for numerical stability by using analytical solutions based on eigenvalue cases. This module also provides a fallback to [`scipy.linalg.logm`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L676) for more complex cases. These mathematical tools leverage PyTorch's tensor capabilities for GPU acceleration and efficient batched computation, supporting complex transformations and analyses within atomistic simulations.

### Advanced Physical Property Calculations
Capabilities for calculating advanced physical quantities and properties in atomistic simulations are provided, encompassing elastic tensor computations, Monte Carlo swap simulations, and specialized correlation analysis functions.

Elastic properties of crystal structures can be determined by analyzing their symmetry and applying a series of precisely chosen deformations. The system then computes stresses using a provided model, ultimately deriving elastic constants and moduli from the stress-strain relationships. Functions such as [`get_bravais_type`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L55) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py) analyze the lattice parameters and angles of a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to classify the crystal system, which is crucial for applying appropriate symmetry constraints during elastic tensor calculations. [`get_elementary_deformations`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L678) then creates [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects representing slightly deformed versions of the crystal, chosen to efficiently sample non-equivalent strain components. The [`calculate_elastic_tensor`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L1105) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py) orchestrates this process, from generating deformations to calculating the full elastic tensor. Finally, [`calculate_elastic_moduli`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L1177) computes common elastic moduli (Bulk modulus, Shear modulus, Poisson's ratio, Pugh's ratio) using Voigt-Reuss-Hill averaging from the derived elastic tensor. For a more detailed understanding of the specific algorithms, refer to [Advanced Physical Property Calculations](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-advanced-physical-property-calculations).

For systems requiring particle exchange or reordering, Monte Carlo (MC) simulations are available. The module [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py) focuses on swap MC in atomic systems, extending the core [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) with MC-specific properties. The [`SwapMCState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py#L37) dataclass manages attributes like system energy and a tensor tracking permutations applied to atoms. The [`generate_swaps`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py#L70) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py) proposes atom swaps between different types within the same system. The [`metropolis_criterion`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py#L157) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py) implements the standard Metropolis acceptance criterion, determining whether to accept or reject proposed moves based on energy differences and temperature. The [`swap_mc_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py#L240) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/monte_carlo.py) advances the simulation by generating and evaluating swaps, ensuring rejected moves are properly reversed. This framework enables the study of phenomena like phase transitions and structural evolution through atom exchanges.

Specialized time correlation functions are provided for in-depth analysis of simulation trajectories. The [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties) directory offers tools for calculating various correlation properties. The [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) class in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py) is designed to compute both auto- and cross-correlation functions for arbitrary simulation properties using efficient FFT-based methods. It tracks multiple properties defined by callable functions and stores historical data in a [`CircularBuffer`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L31) for efficient processing. Building upon this, [`VelocityAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L392) and [`HeatFluxAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L479) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py) provide specialized functionalities for their respective physical quantities, including the calculation of heat flux and the management of running averages. These tools are crucial for deriving transport coefficients and understanding dynamic behavior from MD simulations.

## Model Implementations and Integration
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) framework provides a comprehensive set of models for calculating energies, forces, and stresses in atomistic simulations. These models can be categorized into classical potentials, dispersion and electrostatic models, and wrappers for external machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). All models adhere to a common interface, facilitating their integration and composition.

The core abstraction for all models is the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py). This abstract class establishes a contract that concrete model implementations must fulfill, ensuring a consistent API for computing energy, forces, and optionally stress for a given simulation state. This uniformity allows for generic utilities, such as [`validate_model_outputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L387) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py), which rigorously tests model implementations against the defined interface and physical principles, including correct handling of periodic boundary conditions.

Models can be combined using [`SumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L204) and [`SerialSumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L325), both found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py). [`SumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L204) additively combines the outputs of multiple models, suitable for independent contributions. [`SerialSumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L325) extends this by allowing subsequent models in a sequence to consume features or modified states produced by earlier models, enabling more complex, interdependent potential energy surfaces.

Classical potentials, such as Lennard-Jones, Morse, and Soft Sphere, are implemented within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). These models often build upon the [`PairPotentialModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L277) framework defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py). This framework provides a generic way to define pairwise energy functions, automatically deriving forces via automatic differentiation and calculating virial stresses. For instance, the [`LennardJonesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py#L74) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py) implements the 12-6 potential, while [`MorseModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py#L78) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py) implements the Morse potential. The [`SoftSphereModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L175) and [`SoftSphereMultiModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L248) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py) handle repulsive soft-sphere interactions for single and multiple species, respectively. A specialized [`ParticleLifeModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py#L57) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py) demonstrates an asymmetric force model, inheriting from [`PairForcesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L467) when an explicit energy function is not present.

For long-range interactions, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) includes dispersion and electrostatic models. The [`D3DispersionModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py#L56) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py) provides DFT-D3(BJ) dispersion corrections, leveraging [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) for accelerated computations. Electrostatic interactions are handled by models such as [`DSFCoulombModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L51), [`EwaldModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L156), and [`PMEModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L270), all implemented in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py). These models also rely on [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) for efficient GPU-accelerated calculations, supporting various levels of accuracy for periodic systems.

[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) also offers extensive integration with external machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs). This is achieved through dedicated wrappers that conform to the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), allowing users to seamlessly incorporate state-of-the-art MLIPs into their simulations. Examples include wrappers for MACE ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py)), NequIP/Allegro ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequip_framework.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequip_framework.py)), Allegro via FairChem ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/fairchem.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/fairchem.py)), Mattersim ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mattersim.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mattersim.py)), Metatomic ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/metatomic.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/metatomic.py)), Nequix ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequix.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequix.py)), ORB ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py)), and SevenNet ([`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/sevennet.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/sevennet.py)). These wrappers typically include mechanisms for handling [`ImportError`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L60) gracefully if the external library is not installed, providing a dummy model that raises a clear error upon instantiation.

Finally, the framework provides polarization correction capabilities. The [`UniformPolarizationModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py#L10) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py) calculates additive energy, force, and total polarization corrections under a constant external electric field, utilizing properties stored within the simulation state.

### Model Interface and Composition
The [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py) establishes a foundational contract for all models that calculate energies, forces, and stresses in atomistic simulations. This abstract base class, derived from [`torch.nn.Module`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), requires concrete model implementations to provide a [`forward`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L84) method that accepts a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object and returns a dictionary containing [`"energy"`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L104), [`"forces"`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L904), and optionally [`"stress"`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L905) tensors. It also mandates properties such as [`device`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L418), [`dtype`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L423), [`compute_stress`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L135), and [`compute_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L147), ensuring consistency in how models interact with the simulation framework.

To facilitate the construction of complex potential energy surfaces, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides mechanisms for combining multiple models. The [`SumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L204) class, also defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py), enables the additive composition of child models. When its [`forward`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L84) method is called, it iteratively invokes the [`forward`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L84) method of each child model, summing their canonical mechanical outputs (energy, forces, and stress) into a combined result. Non-canonical outputs from later models in the composition overwrite those from earlier models, following a specific accumulation logic. This design allows for modular development and flexible combination of different interaction types. Building on this, the [`SerialSumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L325) in the same file extends the composition capability by passing an updated [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to subsequent models in the series. This allows models positioned later in the chain to utilize features or modifications introduced by preceding models, supporting more intricate, sequential processing workflows where one model's output influences the input of the next.

Ensuring the correctness and physical adherence of model implementations is crucial. The [`validate_model_outputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L387) utility function, found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py), plays a vital role in this. It rigorously tests [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) implementations against various scenarios, including single and multi-batch systems, and both periodic and non-periodic boundary conditions. This function verifies the presence and correct format of output tensors, checks for non-mutation of the input [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121), and validates that outputs behave as expected under fundamental physical principles, such as consistency during periodic translations. This comprehensive validation process helps guarantee that models conform to the framework's expectations and produce physically sensible results.

### Classical Pair Potentials
Classical pair potentials, such as Lennard-Jones, Morse, and Soft Sphere, are fundamental models for describing interatomic interactions in atomistic simulations. Within TorchSim, these potentials are implemented through generic frameworks like [`PairPotentialModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L277) and [`PairForcesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L467), which are designed to handle batched systems, periodic boundary conditions, and efficient neighbor list generation. These models adhere to the common [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) for energy, force, and stress calculations, enabling their integration into various simulation workflows. See [Model Interface and Composition](#model-implementations-and-integration-model-interface-and-composition) for more details.

The [`PairPotentialModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L277), defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py), is used for potentials that can be expressed as a scalar energy function of pairwise distances. This model automatically derives forces and virial stresses by leveraging PyTorch's automatic differentiation capabilities. For instance, the [`LennardJonesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py#L74) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py) and [`MorseModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py#L78) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py) instantiate [`PairPotentialModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L277) by providing specific energy functions like [`lennard_jones_pair`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py#L23) and [`morse_pair`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/morse.py#L23), respectively. The model efficiently accumulates forces and virial stresses across all interacting pairs, optionally reducing computations for symmetric interactions.

In contrast, the [`PairForcesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L467), also in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py), is utilized when interactions are directly defined by a force magnitude function, without an explicit underlying energy potential. This is particularly useful for modeling non-conservative or asymmetric interactions. The [`ParticleLifeModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py#L57) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py) is an example, where [`particle_life_pair_force`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/particle_life.py#L24) directly calculates force magnitudes. Since there's no energy function, this model explicitly returns zero energies while still computing forces and virial stresses.

Both [`PairPotentialModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L277) and [`PairForcesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/pair_potential.py#L467) manage neighbor list generation using a configurable function, typically [`torchsim_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py#L46), to identify interacting particles within a specified cutoff distance. This ensures that interactions are only computed between relevant atomic pairs, contributing to computational efficiency. They also include robust mechanisms for calculating virial stress, which accounts for the contribution of interatomic forces to the system's stress tensor. The [`SoftSphereModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L175) and [`SoftSphereMultiModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L248) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py) further extend these concepts, providing repulsive soft-sphere potentials for single and multiple atomic species, demonstrating how the generic frameworks can be specialized for different physical interactions.

### Dispersion and Electrostatic Models
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) framework integrates various models to calculate dispersion corrections and electrostatic interactions, crucial components for accurately simulating atomistic systems. These models are designed to be batched-capable, support periodic boundary conditions (PBC), and can compute energy, forces, and virial stress, all while leveraging high-performance kernels from [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) for accelerated execution on GPU/CPU.

For dispersion correction, the [`D3DispersionModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py#L56) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py) implements the DFT-D3(BJ) method. This model processes atomic positions, cell information, and atomic numbers to calculate the dispersion energy and forces. Internally, it handles unit conversions between atomic units and metal units, ensuring consistency with the rest of the simulation. The core calculation is offloaded to the [`nvalchemiops_dftd3`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/dispersion.py#L43) function from the [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) library, which provides optimized implementations for this complex interaction.

Electrostatic interactions are handled by a set of specialized models in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py), each tailored for different computational demands and physical scenarios:
*   The [`DSFCoulombModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L51) calculates Damped Shifted Force (DSF) electrostatics. This method provides an efficient O(N) solution suitable for systems where long-range interactions can be truncated or damped. It utilizes neighbor lists and applies a damping parameter to smoothly cut off Coulomb interactions.
*   The [`EwaldModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L156) implements the classical Ewald summation, a method for computing exact electrostatic interactions in periodic systems. While more computationally intensive (O(N²) or O(N^1.5)), it offers high accuracy for periodic systems. This model requires the system to have periodic boundary conditions; for non-periodic states, it returns zero results.
*   The [`PMEModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L270) (Particle Mesh Ewald) offers an optimized O(N log N) solution for periodic electrostatics, making it computationally more efficient than direct Ewald summation for large systems. It leverages a mesh-based approach to handle long-range interactions efficiently while maintaining accuracy. Like the [`EwaldModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L156), it requires periodic boundary conditions.

All these electrostatic models rely on the presence of [`partial_charges`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L23) within the simulation state and integrate with [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) kernels for their core computations. This integration allows them to benefit from hardware acceleration, particularly on GPUs. The output from [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) is consistently converted to standard metal units (eV/Angstrom) and adjusted for stress tensor sign conventions to align with [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s internal definitions. The common utility function [`_zero_result`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L33) ensures that a consistent output structure is returned even when calculations are bypassed (e.g., for non-periodic systems in [`EwaldModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L156) or [`PMEModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/electrostatics.py#L270)).

These dispersion and electrostatic models adhere to the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py), ensuring a consistent API for energy, force, and stress calculations across all potential models within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). This allows them to be easily composed with other potential models using structures like [`SumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L204) or [`SerialSumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L325). See [Model Interface and Composition](#model-implementations-and-integration-model-interface-and-composition) for details on how models are structured and combined.

### External Machine Learning Potential Wrappers
[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides comprehensive integration with various external machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs), allowing these advanced models to be used seamlessly within its simulation framework. This is achieved through dedicated wrapper classes that conform to the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py). This ensures that MLIPs, regardless of their original implementation, present a consistent API for energy, force, and stress calculations.

Each MLIP integration typically follows a similar pattern. A wrapper class, such as [`MaceModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py#L22) for MACE (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py)), [`NequIPFrameworkModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequip_framework.py#L19) for NequIP and Allegro (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequip_framework.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequip_framework.py)), [`NequixModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequix.py#L20) for Nequix (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequix.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/nequix.py)), [`OrbModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L25) for ORB (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py)), [`SevenNetModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/sevennet.py#L23) for SevenNet (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/sevennet.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/sevennet.py)), [`MatterSimModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mattersim.py#L24) for MatterSim (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mattersim.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mattersim.py)), or [`MetatomicModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/metatomic.py#L20) for metatomic-based models (in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/metatomic.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/metatomic.py)), is defined. These wrappers handle the necessary data transformations between the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object (the universal state representation in [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)) and the input formats expected by the external MLIPs. They also manage the extraction and reformatting of outputs (energies, forces, stresses) from the MLIPs back into [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s standardized dictionary format.

A key design consideration for these integrations is the robust fallback mechanism. Since external MLIPs are often optional dependencies, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) implements a "safe import" pattern. If an external library (e.g., [`mace`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L53), [`nequip`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L59), [`orb-models`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L67)) is not installed, the corresponding wrapper class becomes a dummy placeholder. This dummy class inherits from [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) but will raise an [`ImportError`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L60) immediately upon instantiation, clearly indicating the missing dependency. This prevents hard crashes at import time and provides clear, actionable feedback to the user when they attempt to use a feature that requires an uninstalled external package. For instance, the [`warnings`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L145) module is used to notify developers about failed imports, such as for [`FairChemModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/fairchem.py#L23) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/fairchem.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/fairchem.py).

In addition to basic wrapping, some MLIP integrations include specific model-dependent utilities. For example, the [`OrbModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L25) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py) includes a [`_normalize_charge_spin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L29) static method to ensure that the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) provides required [`charge`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L105) and [`spin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L35) attributes, defaulting them to zero if missing. It also has a [`_get_results`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/orb.py#L42) method to parse raw ORB model outputs, including property renaming and reshaping stress tensors from Voigt notation if necessary. This illustrates how wrappers adapt [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) properties and model outputs to ensure full compatibility.

By conforming to the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), these external MLIP wrappers can be seamlessly integrated into [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s high-level simulation runners, such as [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) and [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638), and leverage features like autobatching and trajectory reporting. More details on the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) and model composition can be found in [Model Interface and Composition](#model-implementations-and-integration-model-interface-and-composition).

### Polarization Correction Models
The [`UniformPolarizationModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py#L10) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py) calculates additive corrections for energy, atomic forces, and total polarization in an atomistic system under a constant external electric field. This model extends the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), ensuring compatibility within the TorchSim framework. It is typically integrated as a component within a larger model, often as part of a [Model Interface and Composition](#model-implementations-and-integration-model-interface-and-composition) chain (e.g., within a [`SerialSumModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L325)).

The model's operation is contingent on the presence of specific properties within the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object, such as [`external_E_field`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L38), [`total_polarization`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L40), and [`polarizability`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L39). For force calculations, [`born_effective_charges`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/typing.py#L24) is also required. If the external electric field is zero, the model returns zero corrections, otherwise, it computes the modifications to energy, polarization, and forces due to the applied field. The [`_finalize_output`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/polarization.py#L63) helper function ensures that output tensors are appropriately detached from the computation graph, managing memory and graph size.

## Simulation Integrators
Molecular dynamics (MD) integrators facilitate the time evolution of atomistic systems under specific thermodynamic conditions. [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides a suite of PyTorch-accelerated MD integrators for batched simulations with periodic boundary conditions, supporting various ensembles, including NVE (microcanonical), NVT (canonical, constant temperature), and NPT (isothermal-isobaric, constant temperature and pressure).

The core of MD simulations revolves around updating particle positions and momenta. The [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) dataclass in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py) serves as the central container for these simulation variables, alongside attributes like energy, forces, masses, cell, and periodic boundary conditions. Fundamental operations such as [`initialize_momenta`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L113) for setting initial velocities, [`momentum_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L169) for updating momenta, and [`position_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L190) for advancing particle positions are also defined here. Many integrators build upon the [`velocity_verlet_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L211), which implements the Velocity Verlet algorithm—a time-reversible and symplectic method for conserving total energy in MD.

The framework manages a wide array of integrators through the [`INTEGRATOR_REGISTRY`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L193) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py). This registry maps each [`Integrator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L125) enum value to its corresponding initialization and stepping functions, enabling dynamic selection and execution of different integration schemes. This design ensures that the specific logic for each ensemble is modularly organized.

Unit conversion is automatically handled for integrator parameters, ensuring consistency and ease of use. The system inspects type hints in integrator function signatures to collect unit metadata, allowing for automatic conversion of user-provided values to internal units. This mechanism, facilitated by [`_collect_unit_kwargs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L231) and [`INTEGRATOR_KWARG_UNITS`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L251) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py), simplifies the interface for users by abstracting away unit management.

For constant temperature simulations, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) offers several NVT integrators, detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py). These include Langevin dynamics, which uses a BAOAB splitting scheme to apply stochastic noise and friction for thermal sampling. Alternatively, the Nose-Hoover chain thermostat, with its [`NVTNoseHooverState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L244), provides a deterministic approach to temperature control. The Velocity Rescaling (CSVR) thermostat, another option, re-scales particle velocities to maintain a target temperature.

For simulations at constant temperature and pressure, the framework provides NPT integrators in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py). These often extend the [`NPTState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L41) to include the system's stress tensor. Implementations include Langevin barostats, which can be configured for anisotropic or isotropic strain control, and Nose-Hoover barostats, which use chains for both temperature and pressure regulation. Additionally, stochastic cell rescaling (C-Rescale) barostats are available for triclinic, anisotropic, and isotropic conditions, offering different approaches to controlling the system's volume and shape. All these integrators leverage [`torch.Tensor`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L90) operations for GPU acceleration, optimizing performance for large-scale simulations.

### Core MD State and Operations
The central component for managing molecular dynamics (MD) simulations is the [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) dataclass, defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py). This class extends the general [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass (see [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management)) and serves as a container for all dynamic variables necessary to describe an atomistic system's state at any given time during an MD simulation. Key attributes include atomic [`momenta`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L62), [`energy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L104), and [`forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L904), alongside inherited properties such as [`positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L177), [`masses`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L178), [`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179), and periodic boundary conditions ([`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180)). [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) also provides computed properties like [`velocities`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L74) and methods for calculating system [`temperature`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L112) and [`kT`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py#L151).

Building upon the [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32), several foundational operations underpin all MD integrators. The [`initialize_momenta`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L113) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py) is responsible for setting the initial velocities of particles by sampling from a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at a specified temperature, ensuring the removal of center-of-mass motion to prevent system drift. This thermalization step is crucial for starting simulations in a physically meaningful state.

The advancement of the simulation through time relies on core stepping functions:
*   [`momentum_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L169): This function, located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py), updates particle momenta based on the forces currently acting on them and the simulation timestep. It also ensures that any defined constraints on momenta are applied.
*   [`position_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L190): Also in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py), this function updates particle positions based on their current velocities and the timestep, incorporating any positional constraints.

These basic steps are combined in the [`velocity_verlet_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L211) function, which implements one full step of the Velocity Verlet integration algorithm. This algorithm is widely used in MD for its accuracy, symplecticity, and time-reversibility, which are important for conserving total energy in microcanonical (NVE) simulations. A single Velocity Verlet step involves a half momentum update, a full position update, a recalculation of forces and energies by the [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71), and a final half momentum update. This sequence ensures that positions, velocities, and forces are consistently advanced. All integrators, including those for NVE, NVT, and NPT ensembles (discussed further in [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators)), build upon these fundamental [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) management and stepping functions.

The Nose-Hoover chain thermostatting mechanism, used for constant temperature simulations, is also defined within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py). This includes the [`NoseHooverChain`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L249) dataclass for storing thermostat state variables and [`NoseHooverChainFns`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L276) for encapsulating associated operations. The [`construct_nose_hoover_chain`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L338) factory function configures the thermostat's behavior based on parameters like relaxation time and chain length, preparing it for integration into NVT and NPT schemes.

### NVE Integrator Implementation
The NVE (microcanonical ensemble) integrator is designed to simulate atomic systems while conserving the total energy. It is implemented within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py) and relies on the core molecular dynamics state management defined in [Core MD State and Operations](#simulation-integrators-core-md-state-and-operations).

The simulation process begins with an initialization function, [`nve_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py#L19), which prepares an [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) for NVE integration. This involves calculating initial potential energies and forces using the designated potential model. If initial momenta (velocities) are not explicitly provided, [`nve_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py#L19) samples them from a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution corresponding to a specified temperature. This ensures the system starts with appropriate kinetic energy while removing any net center-of-mass motion to prevent unintended system drift.

Following initialization, the system's time evolution is managed by the [`nve_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py#L74) function, which performs a single integration step. This function employs the Velocity Verlet algorithm, a numerical integration scheme known for its accuracy, time-reversibility, and conservation properties crucial for microcanonical simulations. The Velocity Verlet algorithm updates particle positions and momenta in a symmetric fashion: a half-step update of momenta, a full-step update of positions, recalculation of forces and potential energy at the new positions, and finally, another half-step update of momenta. This sequence ensures that the total energy of the system remains conserved over long simulation times. Both [`nve_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py#L19) and [`nve_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nve.py#L74) interact with a [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) to abstract the details of force and energy calculations, allowing for flexibility in the choice of interatomic potentials.

### NVT Integrator Implementations
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) framework offers several implementations for NVT (canonical ensemble) integrators, enabling molecular dynamics simulations at constant temperature. These integrators are designed for batched operations and leverage PyTorch for accelerated computations. The available NVT methods include Langevin dynamics, Nose-Hoover Chains (NHC), and Velocity Rescaling (CSVR), each managing the simulation state and advancing the system through distinct integration steps. The choice of integrator impacts how temperature is controlled and how the system samples the canonical ensemble.

Langevin dynamics is implemented using the BAOAB splitting scheme. This method applies both frictional forces and random noise to the particles' momenta, drawing from an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process to ensure proper thermalization. The core steps involve updating momenta, positions, and then applying the stochastic and dissipative forces. The initialization and stepping functions for this method are found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py), specifically [`nvt_langevin_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L89) and [`nvt_langevin_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L145). The underlying [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) (see [Core MD State and Operations](#simulation-integrators-core-md-state-and-operations)) is extended to manage these operations.

For a more deterministic approach to temperature control, Nose-Hoover Chains (NHC) are provided. This method introduces additional fictitious particles (thermostats) that couple to the system's kinetic energy, maintaining the desired temperature without stochastic noise. The NHC implementation in [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) follows Martyna et al.'s direct translation method, employing Suzuki-Yoshida splitting for robust integration of the chain variables. The [`NVTNoseHooverState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L244) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py) extends [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) to incorporate the chain's state variables and helper functions. The [`nvt_nose_hoover_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L293) function initializes the system and the Nose-Hoover chain, while [`nvt_nose_hoover_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L381) orchestrates the evolution of both the physical system and the thermostat chain. The conserved quantity for the NHC ensemble can be calculated using [`nvt_nose_hoover_invariant`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L491) to verify the simulation's correctness.

Finally, Velocity Rescaling (CSVR) offers another method for thermostatting, based on the algorithm proposed by Bussi, Donadio, and Parrinello. This thermostat periodically rescales particle velocities to match the target temperature, incorporating a stochastic component to ensure canonical sampling. The [`NVTVRescaleState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L565) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py) is specialized for this method. The [`_vrescale_update`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L594) function within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py) handles the actual velocity rescaling logic, which is then integrated into the [`nvt_vrescale_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L715) function to advance the simulation.

All NVT integrators leverage a [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) to abstract away force and energy calculations, ensuring flexibility with various potential models. The system's state is encapsulated in [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) or its specialized extensions, facilitating clear management of physical properties and integration variables. The overall selection and setup of these integrators are handled by the [Integrator Registry and Unit Conversion System](#simulation-integrators-integrator-registry-and-unit-conversion-system), which ensures proper unit handling and dynamic selection of integration schemes.

### NPT Integrator Implementations
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) framework includes various NPT (isothermal-isobaric ensemble) integrators within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py) to simulate systems at constant particle number, pressure, and temperature.
