These integrators extend the core [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) with pressure-related attributes and manage cell dynamics in addition to particle motion. The NPT integrators primarily differ in their barostat implementations and how they couple pressure control with temperature control. The core [`NPTState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L41) extends the general [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) by incorporating the [`stress`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L905) tensor, which is crucial for pressure calculations.

**Langevin Barostats**

Two Langevin-based NPT integrators are available, both drawing inspiration from the Gronbech-Jensen & Farago (2014) method and LAMMPS's [`fix press/langevin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L67). These methods introduce additional degrees of freedom to control the system's cell dimensions, similar to how Langevin dynamics controls particle velocities.

*   **Anisotropic Langevin Barostat**: This implementation, utilizing [`NPTLangevinAnisotropicState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L62), manages the simulation cell's shape and volume anisotropically. It introduces logarithmic strain coordinates ([`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108)) for each dimension, along with their corresponding velocities and masses. This allows for independent fluctuations and control over the three lattice vectors. The integration step ([`npt_langevin_anisotropic_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L513)) involves a four-step splitting scheme that updates particle positions and velocities, as well as the cell dimensions, while applying Langevin noise and friction to both particles and the cell coordinates. The force on the cell's strain coordinates is computed from the system's stress, kinetic energy, volume, and external pressure.

*   **Isotropic Langevin Barostat**: The [`NPTLangevinIsotropicState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L653) provides a simplified approach where only the system's volume is controlled, assuming an isotropic scaling of the cell. A single isotropic logarithmic strain coordinate ([`ε`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L154)) dictates the volume change. The [`npt_langevin_isotropic_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L988) integrates the system by isotropically scaling the cell based on this single strain variable, applying similar Langevin dynamics principles to manage the volume fluctuations.

**Nose-Hoover Barostats**

The Nose-Hoover barostat for NPT simulations is implemented using [`NPTNoseHooverIsotropicState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L1110). This method employs Nose-Hoover chains, not only for temperature control but also for pressure control. It extends the concept of a thermostat to a barostat by coupling an additional Nose-Hoover chain to the cell's volume degree of freedom. This implementation typically uses a logarithmic cell coordinate for volume, similar to the isotropic Langevin method. The [`npt_nose_hoover_isotropic_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L1642) function configures two [`NoseHooverChain`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L249) instances: one for the thermostat and another for the barostat. The [`npt_nose_hoover_isotropic_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L1812) uses a symmetric Trotter factorization to integrate the system, handling both particle and cell dynamics, while ensuring the conservation of an extended Hamiltonian. This conserved quantity can be monitored for verifying simulation correctness. For more details on the underlying Nose-Hoover chain mechanics, refer to [Core MD State and Operations](#simulation-integrators-core-md-state-and-operations).

**C-Rescale Barostats**

The C-Rescale barostat, represented by [`NPTCRescaleState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L2062), offers a stochastic cell rescaling approach for NPT simulations. This method is based on Del Tatto et al. (2022) and is particularly useful for controlling cell dynamics under various conditions.

*   **Triclinic C-Rescale Barostat**: The [`_crescale_triclinic_barostat_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L2186) function implements an anisotropic stochastic cell rescaling step for general triclinic cells. It manages volume and deformation updates through a three-step process. The [`npt_crescale_triclinic_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L2517) integrates the system using a Trotter splitting scheme that combines velocity rescaling for temperature control with the triclinic barostat step.

The NPT integrators leverage [`torch.Tensor`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L90) for all numerical computations, enabling efficient GPU acceleration for batched simulations. Each integrator maintains its specific state using [`dataclass`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L13) structures, promoting clear and maintainable code. The overall system for managing integrators and their parameters is described in [Integrator Registry and Unit Conversion System](#simulation-integrators-integrator-registry-and-unit-conversion-system).

### Integrator Registry and Unit Conversion System
The [`INTEGRATOR_REGISTRY`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L193) system facilitates the dynamic selection and initialization of molecular dynamics integrators. This registry, defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py), maps an [`Integrator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L125) enumeration value to a pair of functions: an initialization function ([`init_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L376)) and a stepping function ([`step_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L731)). This structure allows the system to abstract away the specific details of different integration schemes, enabling a unified interface for various NVE, NVT, and NPT simulations.

A robust unit conversion system is integrated to handle physical units consistently across all integrator parameters. This is managed by the [`IntegratorKwargUnits`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L221) dataclass and the [`_collect_unit_kwargs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L231) utility function. The [`_collect_unit_kwargs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L231) function inspects the type hints of an integrator's [`init_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L376) and [`step_fn`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L731) to identify parameters that carry physical units (e.g., time, pressure, inverse time). It then collects their corresponding unit conversion factors, which are stored in [`INTEGRATOR_KWARG_UNITS`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/__init__.py#L251). This pre-calculated dictionary ensures that all integrator parameters are automatically converted to internal units, simplifying user input and preventing errors related to unit inconsistencies.

## Geometry Optimization Algorithms
Optimization algorithms within this repository are designed for batched geometry relaxations of atomic structures. These algorithms update atomic positions and, optionally, cell parameters to minimize the system's energy. A key feature is the filter-based design, which handles various constraints and parameterizations for cell optimization.

The system supports several optimizers, including Gradient Descent, FIRE (Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine), BFGS, and L-BFGS. Each optimizer has dedicated initialization and stepping functions for managing its state and performing iterative updates on batched systems. For instance, [`bfgs_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py#L87) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py) sets up the initial optimization state, including the Hessian matrix, while [`bfgs_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py#L216) performs iterative updates. Similarly, [`fire_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L22) and [`fire_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L117) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py) manage the FIRE algorithm's adaptive timestep and momentum-like updates. The core logic for each optimizer is registered in the [`OPTIM_REGISTRY`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py#L47) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py), allowing for dynamic selection and execution.

Cell optimization is managed through a filter-based design, as detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py). This module defines [`CellFilter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L287) types, such as [`unit`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L290) and [`frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L291), which specify how cell parameters are initialized and updated. These filters calculate cell forces from stress and virial tensors and update cell positions accordingly. For example, [`unit_cell_filter_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L181) initializes the state for the "unit" cell filter, deriving initial [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108) from the deformation gradient. The [`CELL_FILTER_REGISTRY`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L404) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py) provides a mechanism to register and retrieve these different cell filtering methods. This approach enables flexible handling of cell constraints, such as hydrostatic strain or constant volume, and different parameterizations.

The state management for all optimizers, including those handling cell parameters, is unified through a hierarchy of dataclasses in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py). The base [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12) extends [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to include general optimization-related attributes like forces, energy, and stress. Specialized states such as [`FireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L39), [`BFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L55), and [`LBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L102) inherit from [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12) and add algorithm-specific parameters and history tracking. For instance, [`BFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L55) includes the approximate Hessian matrix, while [`LBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L102) maintains histories of displacement and gradient differences for its two-loop recursion. When cell optimization is active, these states are further extended (e.g., [`CellOptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L427), [`CellFireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L458)) to manage cell-specific attributes like [`reference_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L866), [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431), and [`cell_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L438), ensuring consistent context and parameter management throughout the optimization process. For a detailed discussion of state management, see [Optimization State Management and Batched Operations](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-optimization-state-management-and-batched-operations).

### Optimizer Implementations
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository provides a suite of geometry optimization algorithms for the relaxation of atomic structures, designed to operate efficiently on batched systems. These optimizers can handle both position-only minimization and extended optimizations that include cell parameters. The overall design leverages a flexible filter-based mechanism for managing cell constraints and parameterizations.

The available optimization algorithms include:
*   **Gradient Descent:** This is a fundamental optimization algorithm that updates atomic positions based on computed forces and a specified learning rate. It supports cell optimization by updating cell parameters according to a [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431) and a cell-specific learning rate, as detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/gradient_descent.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/gradient_descent.py). Its initialization involves setting up the initial state with forces and energies, while each step updates positions and re-evaluates the model for new forces.
*   **FIRE (Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine):** The FIRE algorithm is implemented to accelerate geometry optimizations. It dynamically adjusts the timestep and a mixing parameter based on the system's "power" (the dot product of forces and velocities), allowing for rapid convergence to energy minima. Two flavors are provided: a Velocity-Verlet based approach and an ASE-mimicking implementation, both managed by [`fire_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L22) and [`fire_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L117) functions in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py). State management for FIRE involves tracking velocities, timestep, and the mixing parameter [`alpha`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L102).
*   **BFGS (Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno):** The BFGS optimizer, found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py), is a quasi-Newton method that approximates the Hessian matrix to determine search directions. It is suitable for systems with a moderate number of atoms where the memory cost of storing a full Hessian per system is manageable. The [`bfgs_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py#L87) function initializes the Hessian and other state variables, while [`bfgs_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py#L216) updates the Hessian approximation, computes the step using eigendecomposition to ensure a descent direction, and applies the update to positions and optionally cell parameters.
*   **L-BFGS (Limited-memory BFGS):** As an alternative to BFGS, L-BFGS (implemented in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/lbfgs.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/lbfgs.py)) offers a more memory-efficient approach by maintaining only a limited history of position and gradient differences instead of a full Hessian. This history is used in a "two-loop recursion" to approximate the inverse Hessian and compute the search direction. [`lbfgs_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/lbfgs.py#L114) sets up the initial state and history tensors, and [`lbfgs_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/lbfgs.py#L262) executes the two-loop recursion, updates positions and cell parameters, and refreshes the history.

All optimizers utilize dedicated state management classes, such as [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12), [`FireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L39), [`BFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L55), and [`LBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L102), which extend the core [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass to include algorithm-specific parameters like forces, energies, velocities, and historical data. When cell optimization is active, specialized states like [`CellOptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L427) or [`CellFireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L458) are employed, which incorporate cell-specific attributes and interact with the [Cell Optimization and Filter-Based Design](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-cell-optimization-and-filter-based-design) mechanisms. These state objects are designed to handle batched systems with varying atom counts efficiently through padding and careful attribute management, as described in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py).

The specific optimizer used can be dynamically selected via the [`OPTIM_REGISTRY`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py#L47), which maps an [`Optimizer`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py#L38) enumeration to its corresponding initialization and step functions, as defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/__init__.py).

### Cell Optimization and Filter-Based Design
Cell optimization within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) utilizes a filter-based design to manage constraints and parameterizations when optimizing unit cell parameters alongside atomic positions during geometry relaxations. This approach is primarily defined and managed within the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py) module.

The system offers two primary [`CellFilter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L287) types: [`unit`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L290) and [`frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L291). These define how the cell's deformation gradient is represented and updated. The [`unit`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L290) filter directly updates the cell based on a deformation gradient where [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108) are a scaled representation. In contrast, the [`frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L291) filter operates in log-space, where [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108) represent the logarithm of the deformation gradient, using functions like [`torch.matrix_exp`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L103) and [`tsm.matrix_log_33`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L463) for conversions.

For each [`CellFilter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L287) type, there are distinct initialization functions, such as [`unit_cell_filter_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L181) and [`frechet_cell_filter_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L230), which set up the initial state for cell optimization. These functions establish properties like the [`reference_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L866) and derive initial [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108). Corresponding step functions, [`unit_cell_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L295) and [`frechet_cell_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L324), then define how the cell parameters are updated in each optimization iteration. These steps involve calculating cell forces from stress and virial tensors via [`compute_cell_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L353) and subsequently adjusting the cell's configuration based on these forces and a learning rate.

The [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431) mechanism allows for flexible handling of cell optimization within various algorithms, including [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms). When a cell filter is active, optimizer states, like [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12), are extended to [`CellOptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L427) (and its specialized derivatives like [`CellFireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L458) or [`CellBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L471)), which incorporate cell-specific attributes such as [`reference_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L866), [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431), [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108), and [`cell_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L438). This enables the management of cell constraints, like [`hydrostatic_strain`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L434) or [`constant_volume`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L435), ensuring that optimization steps adhere to physical or user-defined conditions. A crucial aspect of numerical stability is addressed by functions like [`_clamp_deform_grad_log`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L26), which prevent numerical overflow when large cell deformations occur, particularly relevant for the [`frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L291) method.

### Optimization State Management and Batched Operations
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) optimization framework employs a hierarchical state management system, designed to efficiently handle batched atomistic simulations with varying system sizes and diverse constraints. The foundation of this system is the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass, which encapsulates general atomistic system properties.

Optimization-specific states extend [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to include parameters relevant to the minimization process. The base [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12), defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py), adds attributes like [`forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L904), [`energy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L104), and [`stress`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L905), which are fundamental for any optimization algorithm. A key aspect of [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12) is its [`set_constrained_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L27) method, which ensures that any calculated forces adhere to predefined constraints before being applied, maintaining physical or user-defined boundaries on atomic movement.

Specialized optimization algorithms further extend [`OptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L12) to manage their unique requirements:
*   [`FireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L39), used by the [NVE Integrator Implementation](#simulation-integrators-nve-integrator-implementation), incorporates attributes such as [`velocities`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L74), [`dt`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L46) (timestep), [`alpha`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L102), and [`n_pos`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L48) to manage the adaptive stepping and momentum updates characteristic of the FIRE algorithm.
*   [`BFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L55) maintains the approximate Hessian matrix ([`hessian`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L76)), along with [`prev_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L77) and [`prev_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L78), which are crucial for the BFGS algorithm's iterative updates.
*   [`LBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L102) is designed for the limited-memory BFGS algorithm, storing [`s_history`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L129) (displacement history) and [`y_history`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L130) (gradient-difference history) for its two-loop recursion.

For optimizations involving unit cell parameters, the framework introduces specialized [`CellOptimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L427) dataclasses (e.g., [`CellFireState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L458), [`CellBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L471), [`CellLBFGSState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L499)). These extend their respective base optimizer states with cell-specific attributes, including a [`reference_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L866), [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431) configuration, [`cell_positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L108), and [`cell_forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L438). This enables the simultaneous relaxation of both atomic positions and cell dimensions, while integrating with the filter-based design for cell optimization constraints described in [Cell Optimization and Filter-Based Design](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-cell-optimization-and-filter-based-design).

A critical design consideration for these state objects is their ability to handle batches of systems with varying numbers of atoms. This is achieved through mechanisms like [`_padded_system_attributes`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L98), which identifies attributes requiring padding to [`global_max_atoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/bfgs.py#L124) for efficient batched tensor operations, as detailed in the implementations for [Optimizer Implementations](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-optimizer-implementations) and [Optimizer Implementations](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-optimizer-implementations). This approach allows the framework to perform operations on heterogeneous batches, simplifying tensor computations while maintaining flexibility for different system sizes. The [`atom_idx_in_system`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/state.py#L82) attribute further facilitates the mapping between global padded tensors and individual system data, ensuring accurate per-system updates.

## Neighbor List Algorithms
Neighbor lists are fundamental to atomistic simulations, enabling efficient calculation of interatomic interactions by identifying atoms within a specified cutoff distance. The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository provides multiple implementations for this task, supporting both single and batched system calculations and incorporating an automatic fallback mechanism to leverage the most performant option available.

The system prioritizes accelerated external libraries. If NVIDIA's [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) library is installed, the system uses its GPU-accelerated N² or cell-list algorithms for neighbor searches through the functions in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py). This option offers optimized performance on compatible hardware. If [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) is not available, the system then attempts to use the [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) library. Implementations in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py) provide both a standard Python version ([`vesin_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L36)) and a TorchScript-optimized version ([`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184)) for efficient neighbor list generation. Both Alchemiops and Vesin implementations handle periodic boundary conditions and support batched processing.

As a final fallback, if neither of these external libraries is present, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) includes pure PyTorch implementations in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py). These include an O(N²) brute-force approach ([`torch_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L94)) suitable for smaller systems and a more efficient O(N) linked-cell algorithm ([`torch_nl_linked_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L156)). All neighbor list functions are accessible via a unified entry point, [`torchsim_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py#L46), which automatically selects the most suitable implementation based on environmental availability. This automatic fallback ensures robust functionality across diverse deployment environments.

Beyond simple pairwise interactions, the system also supports the generation of higher-order interaction indices for molecular graphs. Functions within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py) provide pure-PyTorch methods to construct triplets (three-body interactions) and quadruplets (four-body interactions). These are crucial for advanced interatomic potentials and machine learning models that consider angular or dihedral relationships between atoms.

To ensure consistency across these varied implementations, the [`normalize_inputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L7) utility in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py) standardizes the format of cell and periodic boundary condition tensors. This function ensures that inputs are correctly shaped and contiguous, which is vital for efficient processing by the different neighbor list algorithms.

### Automatic Fallback and Prioritization
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) library provides a robust mechanism for automatically selecting the most efficient neighbor list algorithm available on a given system. This ensures optimal performance across diverse hardware configurations without requiring manual intervention from the user. The core logic for this selection resides within the [`torchsim_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py#L46) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py).

The selection process follows a prioritized order:

1.  **Alchemiops**: The system first attempts to utilize NVIDIA's [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) library, which offers highly optimized, GPU-accelerated N² or cell-list neighbor searches. If [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) is detected and available, the [`alchemiops_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py#L35) implementation in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py) is chosen. This provides significant performance gains on compatible NVIDIA GPUs.

2.  **Vesin**: If Alchemiops is not available, the system checks for the [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) library. Two implementations are considered:
    *   **TorchScript-optimized Vesin**: If a TorchScript-compatible version of [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) is installed, [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py) is prioritized. This version offers improved performance through TorchScript optimization.
    *   **Standard Vesin**: If the TorchScript version is not available, the standard [`vesin_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L36) implementation, also in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py), is used. The [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) library provides efficient neighbor list generation for various hardware.

3.  **Pure PyTorch**: As a final fallback, if neither Alchemiops nor Vesin implementations are found, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) defaults to a pure PyTorch solution. The [`torch_nl_linked_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L156) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py) implements an O(N) linked-cell algorithm, which is generally efficient for larger systems. For smaller systems or specific debugging scenarios, an O(N²) brute-force [`torch_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L94) is also available as part of the pure PyTorch offerings.

This hierarchical selection ensures that [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) can always compute neighbor lists, adapting to the available software and hardware resources to maximize efficiency. This automated approach simplifies development and deployment, allowing users to focus on simulation science rather than infrastructure specifics. The [`normalize_inputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L7) utility in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py) plays a supporting role by standardizing the input formats for cell and periodic boundary condition tensors, ensuring compatibility across all chosen neighbor list implementations.

### Alchemiops Neighbor List Implementation
The [`alchemiops_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py#L35) implementation within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) leverages NVIDIA's [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) library to accelerate neighbor list computations, particularly for GPU environments. This approach is part of the system's strategy to prioritize high-performance, hardware-accelerated solutions for neighbor list generation, as outlined in [Automatic Fallback and Prioritization](#neighbor-list-algorithms-automatic-fallback-and-prioritization).

This implementation provides [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) with the capability to perform N² (naive) or cell-list based neighbor searches efficiently, handling batched systems with varying atom counts and supporting periodic boundary conditions. The function accepts atomic [`positions`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L177), [`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179) vectors, [`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180) flags, a [`cutoff`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py#L56) distance, and [`system_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L182) to manage atom ownership in batched scenarios. It returns a mapping of atom pairs, their corresponding system assignments, and the periodic shift indices required to bring neighbors into the primary image of central atoms.

A key aspect of its integration is the handling of self-interactions; [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) typically excludes these by default, so [`alchemiops_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py#L35) explicitly adds self-pairs to the output if the [`self_interaction`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py#L57) flag is set to [`True`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L46). Furthermore, the implementation includes specific logic to address how [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) handles non-periodic systems with zero cell vectors. In such cases, it temporarily substitutes a nominal identity matrix for the zero cell to prevent potential errors within the [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) warp kernels, demonstrating robustness in diverse simulation setups. Input normalization is performed using utilities like [`normalize_inputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L7) found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py) to ensure consistent tensor shapes for [`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179) and [`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180) across [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42) calls.

### Vesin Neighbor List Implementations
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) library provides integrations with the external [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) library for efficient neighbor list calculations, offering both standard Python and TorchScript-optimized versions. These implementations contribute to the automatic fallback mechanism for neighbor list generation, prioritizing performance-optimized external libraries. The primary functions are [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184) and [`vesin_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L36), both located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py).

The [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184) function leverages [`VesinNeighborListTorch`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L28) for TorchScript-compatible environments, enabling potential performance benefits through JIT compilation. The [`vesin_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L36) function uses the standard [`VesinNeighborList`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L18) for environments where TorchScript optimization is not applicable or desired. Both functions require inputs such as atomic positions, cell vectors, periodic boundary conditions (PBC), a cutoff distance, and system indices for batched operations. They handle internal data type and device conversions, ensuring that [`torch.Tensor`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L90) inputs are appropriately processed (e.g., converted to CPU and [`float64`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L273) precision) as required by the [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) library, and results are then converted back to the original device and data type.

These [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) implementations are an integral part of the automatic neighbor list selection process within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). When a neighbor list is requested, the system first checks for the availability of [`nvalchemiops`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L42). If not found, it then attempts to use [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184) if [`VESIN_TORCHSCRIPT_AVAILABLE`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L31) is true. If that is also unavailable, it falls back to [`vesin_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L36) if [`VESIN_AVAILABLE`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L30) is true. This prioritization ensures that the most performant available option is chosen, contributing to the overall efficiency and robustness of simulations. For further details on this selection process, refer to [Automatic Fallback and Prioritization](#neighbor-list-algorithms-automatic-fallback-and-prioritization).

### Pure PyTorch Neighbor List Implementations
The pure PyTorch neighbor list implementations provide reliable fallback mechanisms when highly optimized external libraries, such as those integrated via [`alchemiops_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py#L35) or [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184), are unavailable. These implementations are entirely self-contained within PyTorch, ensuring broad compatibility and avoiding external dependencies. They are particularly relevant for environments where CUDA-enabled hardware or specific [`vesin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/pyproject.toml#L50) installations are not present.

The [`torch_nl_linked_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L156) function, located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py), implements a linked-cell algorithm, offering O(N) complexity for neighbor searching. This approach improves performance scaling for larger systems compared to brute-force methods. For smaller systems or as a simpler alternative, [`torch_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L94) in the same file provides an O(N²) naive brute-force neighbor search. Both functions are designed to handle periodic boundary conditions (PBCs) by first wrapping atomic positions into their primary cells. They then utilize [`strict_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L25) to filter the initial neighborhood based on a precise cutoff distance. The [`shifts_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/transforms.py#L176) are critical in this process, correctly representing the periodic cell shifts between the original, unwrapped input positions and their neighbors. This careful handling of PBCs ensures that interactions across cell boundaries are accurately captured.

The [`torchsim_nl`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py#L46) function, defined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/__init__.py), automatically selects one of these pure PyTorch implementations as a last resort, demonstrating their role as robust fallbacks in the overall neighbor list selection strategy. For additional context on the general neighbor list selection process, refer to [Automatic Fallback and Prioritization](#neighbor-list-algorithms-automatic-fallback-and-prioritization).

### Higher-Order Interaction Indices (Triplets and Quadruplets)
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository provides pure-PyTorch implementations for constructing higher-order interaction indices, which are crucial for modeling multi-body interactions in atomic systems, particularly within machine learning interatomic potentials. These functions are located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py) and are compatible with [`torch.jit.script`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L12), ensuring they can be optimized and deployed efficiently.

The foundation for these operations is the [`_inner_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L41) utility function, which efficiently computes local enumerations within contiguous segments of a sorted tensor. This mechanism is critical for accurately mapping and aggregating data when constructing multi-body interactions.

Three primary functions are available for building these interaction indices:

*   [`build_triplets`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L60) identifies all ordered pairs of edges that share a common target atom, creating a representation of three-body interactions. This is achieved by sorting edges based on their target atom and then using [`_inner_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L41) to generate unique combinations of incoming and outgoing edges for each central atom.
*   [`build_mixed_triplets`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L157) extends this concept by allowing the construction of triplets from two distinct sets of edges. This is useful when different cutoffs or connectivity rules apply to different types of interactions. The function handles filtering of self-loops and incorporates periodic boundary conditions through [`cell_offsets_in`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L162) and [`cell_offsets_out`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L163).
*   [`build_quadruplets`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L243) constructs four-body interaction indices, often visualized as [`d→b→a←c`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L15). This function leverages [`build_mixed_triplets`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L157) to identify initial three-body components and then combines them to form quadruplets. A key aspect of this function is the filtering of degenerate interactions where two atoms might be the same or in the same periodic image, which could represent invalid physical configurations.

These functions provide the means to define and analyze complex atomic environments, supporting advanced potential energy surface representations and graph-based machine learning models. The emphasis on pure-PyTorch implementations ensures flexibility, broad compatibility, and potential for GPU acceleration without relying on external libraries like [`torch_scatter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L4) or [`torch_sparse`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/nbody.py#L5). The utility function [`normalize_inputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L7) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py) plays a role in standardizing input tensor formats for neighbor list calculations, ensuring consistency across different implementations including those that might feed into these higher-order index builders. For a broader understanding of how neighbor lists are generally managed and prioritized, refer to [Automatic Fallback and Prioritization](#neighbor-list-algorithms-automatic-fallback-and-prioritization).

### Input Normalization and Utilities
The [`normalize_inputs`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L7) utility in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py) standardizes the format of simulation cell ([`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179)) and periodic boundary condition ([`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180)) tensors. This function is essential for ensuring consistent input handling across different neighbor list implementations, especially when dealing with batched atomic systems. It prepares these tensors into a uniform [`[n_systems, 3, 3]`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/transforms.py#L27) shape for [`cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L179) and [`[n_systems, 3]`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/transforms.py#L27) for [`pbc`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L180), regardless of their initial input dimensions (e.g., single-system [`[3, 3]`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L141) or [`[3]`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/elastic.py#L790) inputs, or flattened [`[n_systems*3, 3]`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/utils.py#L13) inputs). This normalization step is critical for robust operations within various neighbor list algorithms, ensuring that they receive data in an expected and efficient structure. The function is decorated with [`@torch.jit.script`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/math.py#L12) for potential performance benefits and TorchScript compatibility.

## Simulation Property Calculators
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository provides tools for calculating correlation properties, which are essential for analyzing the dynamics and transport phenomena observed in atomistic simulations. These tools are primarily found in the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties) directory. The core functionality centers around computing time correlation functions for various simulation properties, leveraging PyTorch for efficient, GPU-accelerated calculations using Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT).

The framework includes a general-purpose [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) that can compute both auto- and cross-correlation functions for arbitrary time-dependent data extracted from simulation states. To manage the historical data required for these calculations, an efficient [`CircularBuffer`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L31) is employed, ensuring memory management is optimized during long simulations.

Building upon the [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100), specialized classes are provided for frequently used physical properties. The [`VelocityAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L392) class is designed to compute the Velocity AutoCorrelation Function (VACF), a key quantity for understanding atomic diffusion and vibrational dynamics. Similarly, the [`HeatFluxAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L479) class calculates the Heat Flux AutoCorrelation Function (HFACF), which is crucial for analyzing thermal conductivity. Both specialized calculators manage running averages of their respective correlation functions over multiple simulation windows, allowing for robust statistical analysis.

### General Time Correlation Functions and FFT Acceleration
The [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) class in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py) is designed to compute both auto- and cross-correlation functions for arbitrary simulation properties. It efficiently manages and processes time series data, leveraging FFT-based methods for accelerated computation on various devices supported by PyTorch.

At its core, the [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) utilizes a [`CircularBuffer`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L31) for storing historical data of multiple simulation properties. This buffer, also defined within [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py), is a fixed-size, efficient data structure that prevents frequent memory reallocations, ensuring smooth data handling as new time steps are added. Properties are tracked using user-defined functions that extract relevant [`torch.Tensor`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L90) data from a [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) object at each simulation step.

The process involves updating the calculator with the current simulation state, which then extracts and appends property data to their respective circular buffers. Once sufficient data has accumulated within these buffers, the [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) triggers an FFT-based calculation to determine the auto- and cross-correlation functions. This approach significantly speeds up the computation of correlations compared to direct summation methods, especially for long time series. PyTorch provides the underlying acceleration, allowing these calculations to be performed efficiently on both CPUs and GPUs. The results, including optional normalization, are then stored and can be retrieved for analysis. This general framework also forms the basis for specialized calculators like the [Specialized AutoCorrelation Functions (VACF and HFACF)](#simulation-property-calculators-specialized-autocorrelation-functions-vacf-and-hfacf).

### Specialized AutoCorrelation Functions (VACF and HFACF)
The [`VelocityAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L392) and [`HeatFluxAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L479) classes provide specialized tools for analyzing simulation dynamics by calculating their respective time correlation functions. These classes extend the general capabilities of the [General Time Correlation Functions and FFT Acceleration](#simulation-property-calculators-general-time-correlation-functions-and-fft-acceleration) by focusing on specific physical properties.

[`VelocityAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L392) (found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py)) is designed to compute the velocity autocorrelation function (VACF). It leverages the underlying [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) to track atomic velocities from a simulation state and compute their autocorrelation. This class also supports the accumulation of a running average of the VACF across multiple simulation windows, which is useful for obtaining statistically robust results from molecular dynamics trajectories.

Similarly, [`HeatFluxAutoCorrelation`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L479) (also in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py)) focuses on the heat flux autocorrelation function (HFACF). This involves a more complex calculation, as the heat flux itself needs to be derived from the model's per-atom stresses and energies. Like the VACF calculator, it utilizes the [`CorrelationCalculator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L100) for its core correlation capabilities and manages a running average of the HFACF. This allows for the efficient determination of thermal transport properties from simulation data.

## Example Workflows and Tutorials
[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides a variety of examples, tutorials, and benchmarking tools to guide users through its functionalities for atomistic simulations. These resources demonstrate practical applications of molecular dynamics, structural optimization, phonon calculations, and the use of high-level APIs. The examples also highlight autobatching mechanisms and concepts such as differentiable simulations and provide insights into performance evaluation.

Practical example scripts located in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts) illustrate core [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) features. These include an introduction to basic operations with both classical potentials (e.g., [`LennardJonesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py#L74)) and machine learning potentials (e.g., [`MaceModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py#L22)), covering both single-system and batched simulations as shown in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/1_introduction.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/1_introduction.py). Structural optimization techniques, such as FIRE, Gradient Descent, L-BFGS, and BFGS, are demonstrated with various cell filters in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/2_structural_optimization.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/2_structural_optimization.py). Molecular dynamics simulations across NVE, NVT, and NPT ensembles using different thermostats and barostats are detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/3_dynamics.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/3_dynamics.py). The high-level API, which streamlines complex workflows like MD and geometry optimization, is showcased in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/4_high_level_api.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/4_high_level_api.py), including how to integrate models, utilize trajectory reporting, and define custom convergence criteria. Advanced workflows, such as in-flight autobatching for efficient optimization and the calculation of elastic constants, are presented in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/5_workflow.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/5_workflow.py). Furthermore, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s integration with Phonopy for phonon calculations, including structure relaxation, batched force constant computations, and phonon density of states/band structure analysis, is covered in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/6_phonons.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/6_phonons.py). Additional features, like batched neighbor list calculations and Velocity Autocorrelation Function (VACF) computations, are found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py).

In-depth tutorials in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials) offer guided explanations of key [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) concepts. The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass, which is central to managing atomistic system properties and enables batched operations, is thoroughly explained in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/state_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/state_tutorial.py). This tutorial also covers its creation from external formats and conversion back to them. Tutorials further explore low-level API usage for direct model interaction and manual application of optimizers and integrators, and high-level APIs that orchestrate MD, geometry optimization, and static calculations. The mechanisms of autobatching, including [`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475) and [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768) for managing GPU memory and optimizing batch processing, are detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/autobatching_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/autobatching_tutorial.py). [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms) provides more information on this feature. Trajectory reporting with [`TorchSimTrajectory`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L561) for efficient data storage and retrieval is discussed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reporting_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reporting_tutorial.py). Tutorials also provide guidance on ensuring reproducibility in simulations, addressing non-determinism from GPU operations and stochastic integrators, as demonstrated in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py). [Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-ensuring-reproducibility-in-torchsim) offers further details on this. Differentiable simulations, for instance, for meta-optimization tasks such as finding optimal parameters for a [`SoftSphereMultiModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L248), are illustrated in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/diff_sim.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/diff_sim.py). Hybrid MD/MC methods are also demonstrated, showing how to combine different simulation techniques, as seen in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/hybrid_swap_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/hybrid_swap_tutorial.py).

For performance evaluation, the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking) directory contains scripts that benchmark various aspects of [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). These include molecular dynamics throughput comparisons between [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s batched NVT-Langevin and [`ASE`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24)'s sequential Langevin dynamics in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/md-throughput.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/md-throughput.py). Neighbor list algorithms are benchmarked for efficiency across different implementations (e.g., linked-cell, Alchemiops, Vesin) using random structures from public databases, as shown in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/neighborlists.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/neighborlists.py). The optimization throughput of MACE models using LBFGS or FIRE optimizers is evaluated and compared against [`ASE`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/opt-throughput.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/opt-throughput.py). Finally, [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/scaling.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/scaling.py) assesses [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s scaling performance for static calculations, structural relaxation, NVE, and NVT molecular dynamics across varying numbers of structures. These benchmarking tools help understand the efficiency and performance characteristics of [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) across different use cases and hardware configurations.

### Practical Example Scripts and Their Applications
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository includes a collection of example scripts that demonstrate various applications of the simulation engine, ranging from fundamental setup to advanced workflows. These examples serve as practical guides for users to understand and implement different atomistic simulation tasks.

The foundational principles are introduced in the script located at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/1_introduction.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/1_introduction.py). This script illustrates how to set up [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) objects for single-system and batched simulations and perform basic energy and force calculations using both classical [`LennardJonesModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/lennard_jones.py#L74) and machine learning-based [`MaceModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py#L22) potentials. It highlights how [`system_idx`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L182) is used to manage batched inputs, enabling efficient parallel processing of multiple atomic configurations.

For structural optimization, the script at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/2_structural_optimization.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/2_structural_optimization.py) showcases various algorithms like FIRE, Gradient Descent, L-BFGS, and BFGS. It demonstrates optimizing atomic positions only, as well as joint optimization of positions and the simulation cell using different [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431) options such as [`CellFilter.unit`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L729) and [`CellFilter.frechet`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L86). This allows for various relaxation scenarios, including those involving pressure control.

Molecular dynamics simulations across different thermodynamic ensembles are covered in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/3_dynamics.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/3_dynamics.py). This includes NVE (microcanonical), NVT (canonical with Langevin and Nose-Hoover thermostats), and NPT (isothermal-isobaric with a Nose-Hoover barostat) ensembles. The script illustrates how to set up initial conditions, manage simulation steps, and log thermodynamic properties like temperature and pressure. Further details on these integrators can be found in [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators).

The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) high-level API, designed for streamlined simulation workflows, is demonstrated in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/4_high_level_api.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/4_high_level_api.py). This script shows how to use convenience functions such as [`ts.integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L55) for MD simulations and [`ts.optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L81) for geometry optimizations. It also explains how to configure [`TrajectoryReporter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L68) for logging simulation data and define custom convergence criteria for optimization tasks. For a broader understanding of how these high-level functions orchestrate simulations, refer to [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners).

Advanced simulation workflows are presented in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/5_workflow.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/5_workflow.py). This includes in-flight autobatching for optimizing large sets of structures by dynamically managing batches based on resource availability, which is discussed further in [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms). Additionally, it demonstrates how to calculate elastic constants, including identifying the Bravais lattice type and computing elastic moduli, showcasing advanced physical property calculations as described in [Advanced Physical Property Calculations](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-advanced-physical-property-calculations).

Phonon calculations are detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/6_phonons.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/6_phonons.py). This script outlines a complete workflow from structural relaxation using a [`MaceModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py#L22) to computing phonon density of states (DOS) and band structures using [`Phonopy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24). It highlights the use of batched force constant calculations and the utility functions [`ts.io.state_to_phonopy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L688) and [`ts.io.phonopy_to_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1514) for interoperability with external libraries.

Finally, [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/scripts/7_others.py) explores additional advanced features. This includes batched neighbor list calculations using both linked-cell ([`torch_nl_linked_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L156)) and N² ([`torch_nl_n2`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L94)) methods, as described in [Neighbor List Algorithms](#neighbor-list-algorithms). It also demonstrates how to compute the Velocity Autocorrelation Function (VACF) during an NVE molecular dynamics simulation, further illustrating the capabilities described in [Simulation Property Calculators](#simulation-property-calculators).

### In-Depth Tutorials for Key Features
Tutorials in [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) guide users through core functionalities, from fundamental [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) management to advanced simulation techniques. These examples demonstrate how to create, manipulate, and interconvert system states with external atomistic libraries. The core data structure, [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121), handles atomistic system properties for single or batched systems. Tutorials illustrate [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) creation using [`initialize_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1480) from formats like [`ASE`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24) [`Atoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L26), [`Pymatgen`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24) [`Structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L10), and [`Phonopy`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24) [`PhonopyAtoms`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/io.py#L5). The [`to`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L730) method manages data types and device placement, while methods like [`clone`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L591), [`pop`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L701), [`split`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L690), and [`concatenate_states`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L1317) facilitate state manipulation. For molecular dynamics, the [`MDState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L32) subclass extends [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) with properties like [`momenta`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/md.py#L62) and [`forces`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L904). For more details, see [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management).

[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides both low-level and high-level APIs. The low-level API is detailed in the tutorial located at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/low_level_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/low_level_tutorial.py). This tutorial shows how to directly interact with models, such as [`MaceModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/mace.py#L22), to compute energy, forces, and stress, and manually apply optimizers (e.g., FIRE via [`fire_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L22) and [`fire_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/fire.py#L117)) and integrators (e.g., NVT Langevin via [`nvt_langevin_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L89) and [`nvt_langevin_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/nvt.py#L145)). This approach offers fine-grained control for users to implement custom simulation loops. The high-level API, demonstrated in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/high_level_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/high_level_tutorial.py), simplifies common simulation tasks through functions like [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) for molecular dynamics, [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) for geometry optimization, and [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844) for single-point calculations. These functions support various integrators and optimizers and include features for trajectory reporting and autobatching. See [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) for further context.

Autobatching strategies are critical for efficient GPU memory management when simulating multiple systems. The tutorial at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/autobatching_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/autobatching_tutorial.py) explains how [`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475) groups states using a binpacking algorithm for fixed-iteration workflows, while [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768) provides dynamic batching for tasks like geometry optimization, where states converge at different rates. These mechanisms help maintain high GPU utilization. Refer to [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms) for a deeper understanding.

Trajectory reporting is handled by [`TorchSimTrajectory`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L561) for low-level HDF5 file interaction and [`TrajectoryReporter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L68) for high-level data recording. The tutorial at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reporting_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reporting_tutorial.py) illustrates how to save simulation data, including custom properties, to HDF5 files. The [`TrajectoryReporter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L68) supports custom property calculators, allowing users to log specific quantities at defined frequencies.

Reproducible restarts are crucial for simulation integrity. The tutorial in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py) demonstrates how to save and restore the complete simulation state, including the [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40) random number generator state, to ensure exact reproducibility, especially for stochastic integrators. This involves comparing trajectories and final RNG states between continuous and restarted simulations to verify identical results.

Differentiable simulations enable meta-optimization. The tutorial at [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/diff_sim.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/diff_sim.py) shows how [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) can be used to reproduce a bubble raft example, finding an optimal particle diameter by minimizing potential energy through gradient descent. This involves leveraging [`torch.autograd.grad`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/diff_sim.py#L273) to calculate gradients of the final energy with respect to simulation parameters, making the simulation process itself differentiable.

Finally, [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) supports hybrid simulation methods.
