The tutorial in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/hybrid_swap_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/hybrid_swap_tutorial.py) demonstrates combining molecular dynamics with Monte Carlo, specifically NVT Langevin MD with Swap Monte Carlo. This showcases the modularity of [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) components, allowing for custom state objects and alternating between different integrators to build complex simulation workflows.

### Benchmarking for Performance Evaluation
[`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) provides a dedicated suite of tools and methodologies for benchmarking its performance across various simulation types, offering insights into throughput, efficiency, and scaling behavior. These benchmarks are crucial for evaluating optimizations, comparing different algorithms, and understanding the library's capabilities relative to external baselines like ASE (Atomic Simulation Environment). The benchmarking scripts are located in the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking) directory.

The benchmarking suite covers several key areas:

*   **Molecular Dynamics (MD) Throughput**: The [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/md-throughput.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/md-throughput.py) script assesses the performance of MD simulations, specifically comparing [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s batched NVT-Langevin dynamics with ASE's sequential Langevin dynamics. This benchmark evaluates how efficiently [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) utilizes GPUs for parallel simulations, measuring systems processed per unit time. It also provides a baseline by benchmarking raw model forward pass throughput, which is essential for understanding the intrinsic speed of the underlying interatomic potentials.

*   **Neighbor List (NL) Algorithm Efficiency**: The [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/neighborlists.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/neighborlists.py) script focuses on the performance of different neighbor list implementations within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). It compares algorithms such as [`torch_nl_linked_cell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/torch_nl.py#L156), [`vesin_nl_ts`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/vesin.py#L184), and [`alchemiops_nl_cell_list`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/neighbors/alchemiops.py#L106). By testing these against various crystal structures sourced from public databases, the benchmark quantifies the computational cost of identifying interacting atoms, which is often a bottleneck in large-scale simulations. This helps in selecting the most performant NL strategy for a given system and hardware.

*   **Optimization Throughput**: Geometry optimization, a common task in atomistic simulations, is benchmarked using the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/opt-throughput.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/opt-throughput.py) script. This benchmark measures the rate at which [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s LBFGS or FIRE optimizers can relax structures to a specified force tolerance, comparing its batched approach against ASE's sequential optimization. The use of [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768) (as seen in [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms)) is critical here, enabling dynamic batching and efficient resource allocation for optimizing diverse structures concurrently.

*   **Scaling Performance**: The [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/scaling.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/benchmarking/scaling.py) script evaluates how [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s performance scales with an increasing number of simulated structures for various tasks, including static calculations, structural relaxations, and NVE/NVT molecular dynamics. This benchmark provides insights into the efficiency of [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3)'s parallelization and batching mechanisms (such as [`BinningAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L475) and [`InFlightAutoBatcher`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/autobatching.py#L768)), demonstrating its ability to maintain performance as the computational load increases.

These benchmarks provide a robust framework for performance evaluation, ensuring that [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) remains performant and efficient for a wide range of atomistic simulation tasks. The results inform development decisions and highlight areas for further optimization. For practical examples of simulation setup and execution, refer to [Practical Example Scripts and Their Applications](#example-workflows-and-tutorials-practical-example-scripts-and-their-applications) and [In-Depth Tutorials for Key Features](#example-workflows-and-tutorials-in-depth-tutorials-for-key-features).

## Advanced Workflows and Research Applications
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository includes advanced workflows and research showcases, particularly focusing on methods for atomic structure generation, optimization, and validation within the [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows) directory. A key application demonstrated is the Atomistic to Continuum (A2C) crystallization workflow, reimplemented within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3).

This framework provides utilities for generating initial atomic configurations, including random packing of single and multi-species systems, which is crucial for exploring new material structures. Overlap minimization during this generation process is achieved using soft-sphere potentials and the Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine (FIRE) algorithm. The [`min_distance`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L26) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) is used to detect atomic overlaps, while [`get_diameter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L73) and [`get_diameter_matrix`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L140) functions in the same file help parameterize the soft-sphere models based on elemental properties.

The workflows also support various modes of structural relaxation, including fixed-cell, unit-cell, and Frechet-cell optimizations, leveraging the [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms) provided by [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). For instance, [`get_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L829), [`get_unit_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L684), and [`get_frechet_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L756) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) implement these different relaxation types using the FIRE optimizer.

A significant aspect of the crystallization workflow involves [`get_subcells_to_crystallize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L504) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py), which extracts smaller subcells from a larger structure for independent processing. These extracted subcells can then be converted into distinct structural units using [`subcells_to_structures`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L616). The [`valid_subcell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L434) function is used for validating relaxed structures against criteria such as formation energy, energy reduction during optimization, and the absence of atomic fusion.

The A2C method, detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/readme.md`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/readme.md), integrates these components to enable a comprehensive crystallization workflow from initial structure generation and optimization through subcell extraction, relaxation, and validation. The implementation leverages PyTorch tensors for underlying computations, enabling GPU acceleration for performance.

### Atomistic Structure Generation and Optimization
The [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3) repository includes methods for generating and optimizing atomic structures, which are central to various computational materials science workflows, particularly crystallization. These methods leverage PyTorch tensors for underlying computations, allowing for GPU acceleration.

A foundational aspect of structure generation involves minimizing atomic overlaps. This is achieved using a soft-sphere potential, implemented through [`SoftSphereModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L175) and [`SoftSphereMultiModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L248). These models describe repulsive interactions between atoms, preventing them from occupying the same space. The parameters for these potentials, such as atomic diameters, are estimated dynamically based on elemental properties derived from [`Pymatgen`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24)'s [`Composition`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L16) class, considering factors like metallic, atomic, and ionic radii.

For instance, initial atomic configurations can be created using functions like [`random_packed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L210) (for single-species systems) and [`random_packed_structure_multi`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L315) (for multi-species systems) found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py). These functions randomly place atoms within a simulation cell and then use an optimization algorithm to relieve overlaps by minimizing the soft-sphere potential energy.

The primary algorithm employed for geometry optimization across various scenarios is the Fast Inertial Relaxation Engine (FIRE). This algorithm is known for its efficiency in finding local energy minima. Within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3), FIRE is integrated through functions such as [`ts.fire_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L298) and [`ts.fire_step`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L308) (as utilized in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py)).

The framework supports different types of structural relaxation depending on whether the unit cell parameters are allowed to change:
*   **Fixed Cell Relaxation**: Atomic positions are optimized while the unit cell dimensions remain constant.
*   **Unit Cell Relaxation**: Both atomic positions and the unit cell parameters are optimized, allowing the cell shape and volume to adapt to the minimum energy configuration.
*   **Frechet Cell Relaxation**: Similar to unit cell relaxation, but specifically uses the Frechet metric to guide cell parameter changes.

These relaxation capabilities, found in functions like [`get_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L829), [`get_unit_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L684), and [`get_frechet_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L756) in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py), use a [`ModelInterface`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/interface.py#L71) to compute forces and stresses. The choice between these relaxation types is managed through the [`cell_filter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/optimizers/cell_filters.py#L431) parameter in the [`ts.fire_init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L298) function. For a deeper understanding of these optimizers, refer to [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms).

### Subcell Extraction and Structural Validation
Subcells can be extracted from larger atomic structures, such as those generated from a random packed configuration. The [`get_subcells_to_crystallize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L504) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) systematically identifies these subcells using a grid-based approach. This function allows for constraints on compositional purity and atom count, ensuring that extracted subcells are chemically relevant. Once identified, the [`subcells_to_structures`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L616) function, also found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py), converts these subcell indices and their boundaries into distinct structure tuples.

After extraction, these structures undergo validation to ensure their physical plausibility and the success of any prior optimization steps. The [`valid_subcell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L434) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) performs this validation by checking criteria such as the formation energy, the energy reduction achieved during relaxation, and the absence of atomic fusion (i.e., atoms being too close to each other). The [`min_distance`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L26) function in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) is used to confirm that no atoms are unphysically close, which is a critical aspect of structural integrity. These validation steps help filter out unphysical or poorly optimized structures, retaining only those suitable for further analysis or downstream applications within workflows such as the [Crystallization Workflow with A2C Method](#advanced-workflows-and-research-applications-crystallization-workflow-with-a2c-method).

### Crystallization Workflow with A2C Method
The [`A2C`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/readme.md#L3) (Atomistic to Continuum) method provides a complete workflow for crystallization, enabling the generation, optimization, and validation of atomic structures within [`torch-sim`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L3). This workflow is primarily implemented in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py) and is designed to be a reproducible research showcase as detailed in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/readme.md`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/readme.md).

The process begins with generating initial atomic structures. For single-species systems, [`random_packed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L210) generates random atomic positions, minimizing overlaps using a [Classical Pair Potentials](#model-implementations-and-integration-classical-pair-potentials) and the [Optimizer Implementations](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-optimizer-implementations). This functionality is extended to multi-species systems by [`random_packed_structure_multi`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L315), which utilizes a [`SoftSphereMultiModel`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/models/soft_sphere.py#L248) and a diameter matrix to handle species-specific interactions. The [`min_distance`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L26) function, which leverages [`transforms.get_pair_displacements`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L56) to calculate pairwise distances under periodic boundary conditions, plays a crucial role in detecting atomic overlaps. Atomic diameters for soft-sphere potentials are estimated using [`get_diameter`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L73) and [`get_diameter_matrix`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L140), drawing on elemental properties from [`Pymatgen`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L24)'s [`Composition`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L16) class.

Once initial structures are generated, the workflow proceeds to subcell extraction and conversion. [`get_subcells_to_crystallize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L504) systematically extracts smaller subcells from a larger structure using a grid-based approach. This function supports compositional and atom count restrictions, allowing the workflow to focus on chemically relevant stoichiometries. The extracted subcell indices are then converted into distinct structure tuples by [`subcells_to_structures`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L616) for further processing.

Structural relaxation is a key component, employing the [Optimizer Implementations](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-optimizer-implementations) for all geometry optimizations due to its efficiency. [`get_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L829) performs atomic position relaxation with fixed cell parameters. For scenarios requiring cell changes, [`get_unit_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L684) relaxes both atomic positions and unit cell parameters while preserving the overall unit cell shape, while [`get_frechet_cell_relaxed_structure`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L756) uses the Frechet metric for cell changes. These functions demonstrate how different [Cell Optimization and Filter-Based Design](#geometry-optimization-algorithms-cell-optimization-and-filter-based-design) can be applied.

Finally, structure validation is performed by [`valid_subcell`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L434), which checks relaxed structures against criteria such as physically reasonable formation energy, successful energy reduction during optimization, and the absence of atomic fusion. The [`get_target_temperature`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/workflows/a2c.py#L660) function provides a temperature profile for melt-quench simulations, completing the crystallization workflow.

## User Guide to Core Concepts
TorchSim provides a set of fundamental concepts designed to streamline atomistic simulations. At its core, the library offers high-level simulation runners, a unified state management system, automatic batching for performance optimization, robust trajectory reporting, and explicit mechanisms for ensuring reproducibility.

The primary entry points for executing simulations are the high-level runner functions: [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317), [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638), and [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844). The [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) function orchestrates molecular dynamics simulations (e.g., NVT, NPT), handling time-evolution of atomic systems. The [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) function is used for geometry relaxations, driving atomic structures towards stable configurations. Finally, the [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844) function performs single-point calculations, evaluating properties of a static atomic configuration. These runners share a consistent interface, abstracting away much of the underlying complexity and supporting various interatomic potential models and external I/O operations, all while operating within the [`metal`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L150) unit system. See [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) for more details.

Central to TorchSim's design is the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass, which serves as the universal container for atomistic system properties. All attributes within [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) are represented as PyTorch tensors, facilitating direct and efficient GPU computation. This data structure supports batched operations, allowing multiple simulation systems to be processed concurrently. Specialized [`State`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L10) types, such as those for NVT Langevin dynamics or Frechet cell optimization, extend [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) to incorporate specific simulation parameters and behaviors. This architecture ensures that integrators, optimizers, and potential models can directly operate on these batched states, maximizing GPU efficiency. See [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management) and [Core `SimState` Data Structure and Batched Operations](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-core-simstate-data-structure-and-batched-operations) for further information.

To manage computational resources effectively, especially GPU memory, TorchSim incorporates automatic batching mechanisms. These mechanisms dynamically optimize batch sizes based on factors like model memory footprints and neighbor list computation methods. This ensures efficient execution, whether for fixed-time molecular dynamics runs or for optimization tasks where systems may converge and be removed from active batches. This dynamic batching extends to trajectory reporting, maintaining performance across diverse simulation scenarios. For a deeper understanding of this functionality, refer to [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms) and [Automatic Batching for Performance](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-automatic-batching-for-performance).

Simulation data, including atomic positions, velocities, energies, and other properties, are efficiently recorded using the [`TorchSimTrajectory`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L561) format. Built upon HDF5, this format provides an optimized container for storing and retrieving time-series data from simulations. It offers native integration with TorchSim's batched states, supports binary encoding of properties, and includes on-the-fly compression, making it suitable for managing large datasets generated during long-running simulations. More details can be found in [Trajectory Reporting with `TorchSimTrajectory`](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-trajectory-reporting-with-torchsimtrajectory).

Achieving reproducibility in atomistic simulations, particularly those involving stochastic elements or GPU acceleration, is a critical concern. TorchSim addresses this by providing explicit guidance and mechanisms to ensure deterministic simulation trajectories. This involves configuring the PyTorch environment for determinism and, crucially, explicitly seeding the [`torch.Generator()`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44) embedded within [`SimState.rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44). This generator controls stochastic processes such as initial momenta sampling and per-step noise in integrators like NVT Langevin. While deterministic integrators do not inherently require seeding, consistent batch composition is necessary for reproducibility across batched simulations. For detailed steps on how to achieve reproducible restarts, including serialization and restoration of the full simulation state, consult [Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-ensuring-reproducibility-in-torchsim) and the example in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py).

### Core `SimState` Data Structure and Batched Operations
The [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) dataclass serves as the central data structure within TorchSim for encapsulating atomistic system properties. It stores information such as atomic numbers, cell parameters, and other simulation variables, with all attributes represented as PyTorch tensors. This design is crucial for leveraging PyTorch's capabilities, enabling mathematical operations performed by integrators and optimizers, as well as model forward passes, to act directly on these tensors, thereby optimizing GPU performance.

[`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) supports batched operations, allowing it to represent either a single system or a collection of multiple systems simultaneously. This batched approach is fundamental to TorchSim's efficiency in handling concurrent simulations. Specific simulation types, such as NVT Langevin or Frechet cell fire, utilize their own specialized [`State`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L10) types that inherit from [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121). Each of these derived [`State`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L10) types includes unique initialization and update functions tailored to its particular simulation context.

This architecture forms the basis for how TorchSim manages its high-level runner functions, including [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317), [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638), and [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844). These runners wrap the underlying functional approach, which involves integrators and optimizers operating on these [`State`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L10) objects via [`init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L271) and [`update`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L179) functions. Further details on how these runners orchestrate simulations are available in [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) and [High-Level Simulation Runner Functions](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-high-level-simulation-runner-functions). The ability to manage batched states efficiently is also a cornerstone for TorchSim's [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms), which dynamically optimizes GPU memory usage.

For ensuring reproducible simulations, [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) contains an explicit [`torch.Generator()`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44) in its [`rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L214) attribute. Users must explicitly seed [`sim_state.rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/testing.py#L207) to ensure deterministic trajectories, as global PyTorch seeds alone are insufficient. More information on achieving reproducibility can be found in [Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-ensuring-reproducibility-in-torchsim).

### High-Level Simulation Runner Functions
TorchSim provides high-level runner functions—[`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317), [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638), and [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844)—designed to orchestrate various atomistic simulations. These functions serve as a unified interface for conducting molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, geometry optimizations, and single-point calculations, respectively. They are built upon TorchSim's modular functional architecture, which employs specialized [`init`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/CHANGELOG.md#L271) and [`update`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/properties/correlations.py#L179) functions that operate on unique [`State`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L10) objects, ultimately inheriting from [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) [Core Simulation State Management](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-core-simulation-state-management).

The [`integrate`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L317) function is primarily used for MD simulations, enabling the propagation of atomic systems through time using various integrators, such as those for the NVE, NVT, and NPT ensembles [Simulation Integrators](#simulation-integrators). For instance, it can handle Langevin dynamics or Nose-Hoover chains, as described in [NVT Integrator Implementations](#simulation-integrators-nvt-integrator-implementations), or NPT barostats [NPT Integrator Implementations](#simulation-integrators-npt-integrator-implementations). The [`optimize`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L638) function is tailored for geometry optimizations, supporting algorithms like Gradient Descent, BFGS, L-BFGS, and FIRE to find stable atomic configurations [Geometry Optimization Algorithms](#geometry-optimization-algorithms). The [`static`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/runners.py#L844) function, on the other hand, performs single-point calculations, evaluating energy, forces, and other properties for a given atomic structure without time evolution or optimization.

These high-level runners share a consistent interface, supporting a diverse range of models for energy, force, and stress calculations, including classical potentials and wrappers for external machine learning potentials [Model Implementations and Integration](#model-implementations-and-integration). They also facilitate compatibility with external I/O formats, ensuring interoperability with other simulation tools. A key feature is their support for automatic batching, which efficiently manages GPU memory and optimizes computations for varying system sizes and model complexities [Autobatching Mechanisms](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-autobatching-mechanisms). This allows for processing multiple simulation states concurrently, improving computational throughput. Additionally, these runners are integrated with [`TorchSimTrajectory`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L561) for efficient trajectory reporting, storing simulation data in an [`HDF5`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L24)-based format that supports binary encoding and on-the-fly compression [Trajectory Reporting with `TorchSimTrajectory`](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-trajectory-reporting-with-torchsimtrajectory). All calculations performed by these runners adhere to the [`metal`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/units.py#L150) unit system. Further details on their operation and best practices can be found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md). For information regarding achieving deterministic behavior in simulations using these runners, refer to [Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-ensuring-reproducibility-in-torchsim).

### Automatic Batching for Performance
TorchSim incorporates automatic batching mechanisms to optimize GPU memory utilization and processing efficiency for diverse simulation scenarios. This system dynamically manages how multiple atomistic systems are grouped and processed, particularly when dealing with varied memory footprints arising from different machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) or neighbor list computation methods. For instance, some MLIPs like MACE exhibit memory scaling that depends on both the number of atoms and system density, while others, such as Fairchem, scale with the maximum number of neighbors. The autobatching system intelligently accounts for these differences.

The core function of this automatic batching is to determine the optimal packing of systems onto the GPU to maximize throughput. It ensures that the GPU's computational resources are efficiently leveraged, irrespective of the system sizes or the specific models being employed. This optimization extends to both fixed-time molecular dynamics simulations and geometry optimization runs. In optimization tasks, where systems converge and are subsequently removed from the active batch, the autobatching dynamically reconfigures the batch to maintain efficiency. This dynamic management also facilitates efficient trajectory reporting, ensuring that simulation data is captured and stored without hindering performance. For further details on how simulation states are managed in conjunction with autobatching, refer to [Core `SimState` Data Structure and Batched Operations](#user-guide-to-core-concepts-core-simstate-data-structure-and-batched-operations).

### Trajectory Reporting with `TorchSimTrajectory`
The [`TorchSimTrajectory`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L561) format facilitates the storage and retrieval of simulation data. Built upon [`HDF5`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md#L24), this format efficiently captures trajectory information by natively integrating with batched states within TorchSim. It supports binary encoding of properties and on-the-fly compression for various data points, such as positions, velocities, temperatures, forces, and per-atom energies, as described in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/overview.md). This system enables efficient tracking of simulation progress and detailed post-analysis, complementing the [High-Level Simulation Runners](#atomistic-simulation-engine-core-high-level-simulation-runners) that orchestrate the simulations.

### Ensuring Reproducibility in TorchSim
Achieving deterministic behavior in molecular dynamics simulations within TorchSim requires careful management of random number generation and system states, especially given the presence of stochastic integrators and potential non-deterministic GPU operations. While exact reproducibility is not always critical for tasks focused on sampling and ensemble statistics, it becomes essential when repeatable trajectories are desired, for instance, during debugging or when comparing specific simulation runs.

TorchSim provides mechanisms to ensure determinism by requiring explicit seeding of the [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121). Unlike global PyTorch seeding mechanisms, TorchSim internally uses an explicit [`torch.Generator()`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44) in [`SimState.rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L44), which is independent of the global seed. Therefore, users must explicitly seed their [`SimState`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L121) via [`sim_state.rng = 42`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/testing.py#L18) to ensure deterministic trajectories. This is particularly important for stochastic integrators, such as [`ts.Integrator.nvt_langevin`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/README.md#L61) and [`ts.Integrator.npt_langevin_anisotropic`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L53), which incorporate random terms but will produce identical trajectories when [`state.rng`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/integrators/npt.py#L37) is consistently seeded. For algorithmically deterministic integrators, like [`ts.Integrator.nvt_nose_hoover`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L56) and [`ts.Integrator.nve`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L56), explicit seeding is not required for their inherent operations, as they do not introduce stochastic terms.

When performing batched simulations, reproducibility also depends on the batch composition. Since all systems in a batch share a single [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40), maintaining identical batch composition—meaning the same systems in the same order—is necessary for exact reproducibility. Any changes to the batch composition will alter the consumption of random numbers and lead to divergence in trajectories.

For reproducible restarts, the complete simulation state, including the [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40)'s state, must be serialized and reloaded. While a simple [`torch.save`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L84) of the full state dictionary might work for [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40) objects in recent PyTorch versions (with [`weights_only=False`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L93)), a more robust and portable method involves saving the RNG state as a plain [`uint8`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md#L99) tensor using [`get_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/trajectory.py#L1202) and restoring it by creating a new [`torch.Generator`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L40) and setting its state with [`set_state`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/torch_sim/state.py#L54). This approach avoids potential pickle incompatibilities across different PyTorch versions. A complete example demonstrating this process can be found in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/examples/tutorials/reproducible_restart_tutorial.py). Further details on global deterministic setup in PyTorch, including environment variables and seeding of various random number generators, are outlined in [`/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md`](https://github.com/torchsim/torch-sim/docs/user/reproducibility.md). A broader overview of TorchSim's core concepts, including its state management and auto-batching, is available in [User Guide to Core Concepts](#user-guide-to-core-concepts).
